title: OTWD change
description: A change applied to the live data, as it appears in the change feed (GET /v1/changes), in change webhooks and in delta files. It covers every record type and names the record in record_id. kind says what the change did to the record and origin says why it happened: most changes apply an approved submission (without naming it), and the others revert an earlier change, carry out a takedown or recompute derived values (ADR 0036). Sequence numbers are global, strictly increasing in the order changes are applied, and never reused. They may have gaps, so use previous_seq to detect a missed change to one record. The change feed is retained for 90 days, and a consumer that falls further behind starts again from a full bulk download.

seq.description: This change's sequence number, which also becomes the record's change_seq.

record_id.description: The record changed, of any record type. Skip a change to a record type you do not know.

kind.description: What the change did to the record. record_created: a new record. facts_updated: facts or facilities set or removed. facts_confirmed: contributors confirmed facts are still true, so their confirmations changed and their values did not. photo_added and photo_removed: a photo of the record published or taken down. status_changed: a closure, temporary closure or reopening. record_merged: the record became a duplicate and now redirects to merged_into. record_unmerged: a wrongly merged record became a record again, separate from unmerged_from. record_split: part of the record became new records of the same type, named in split_into, and the record keeps the rest. record_replaced: the record turned out to be another record type and now redirects to replaced_by. record_retracted: the record should never have been published and only its stub remains. derived_updated: derived values were recomputed. Open: a consumer that meets a kind it does not know fetches the record again, using changed_fields to see what moved.

origin.description: Why the change happened. submission: a moderation decision approved a submission. revert: a moderator undid an earlier change, named in reverts_seq, for example after an appeal or when an abused API key's changes are reverted in bulk. takedown: a moderator removed content for a reason in takedown_reason, such as personal information or a copyright claim. Who asked for a takedown is never published. recompute: OTWD recomputed derived values, for example after a boundary dataset was updated, with no decision because no fact changed. Open: a consumer treats a change of an origin it does not know like any other change.

previous_seq.description: The record's change_seq before this change. Absent for record_created. A consumer that does not hold this sequence for the record has missed a change and should fetch the record again.

changed_fields.description: JSON Pointers to the parts of the record this change set, removed or confirmed, for example /facts/prices, /facts/vertical_clearance, /facilities/power, /status or /photos.

anyOf.description: Parts of the record outside facts and facilities.

removed_fields.description: The subset of changed_fields that the change removed.

safety_fact_changed.description: True when any changed field is a safety fact, so partner apps can refresh those first. The fixed checks derive it from the record type's safety facts, so it is never false when a safety fact changed.

merged_into.description: For record_merged: the surviving record, of the same record type.

unmerged_from.description: For record_unmerged: the record this one had been merged into, of the same record type.

split_into.description: For record_split: the new records made from part of this one, of the same record type. Each has its own record_created change naming this record in split_from.

split_from.description: For a record_created that comes from a split: the record it was split from.

replaced_by.description: For record_replaced: the record of another record type that replaces this one.

reverts_seq.description: For origin revert: the change this one undoes. The facts it touched return to their values and provenance before that change, with this change's sequence number as their change_seq.

takedown_reason.description: For origin takedown: why the content was removed. personal_information: it identified a person. copyright: it was not the contributor's to license. legal_requirement: a law or court order required it. offensive_content: abusive or offensive text or images. private_property: it disclosed a private place without permission. Open: a consumer shows the change without a reason it does not know.

recompute_reason.description: For origin recompute: what made OTWD recompute. boundary_update: a boundary dataset, such as subdivisions, localities or time zones, was updated. tz_database_update: a new release of the IANA time zone database. geometry_reprocessed: the length of a line was measured again. Open: a consumer shows the change without a reason it does not know.

decision_id.description: The moderation decision behind the change. Absent for origin recompute, which no one decides. Changes never name the submission, so the change feed cannot be joined to who submitted (ADR 0038). A partner app finds the changes its own submissions produced in their status.

allOf.description: record_merged names merged_into, and no other kind does.
record_unmerged names unmerged_from, and no other kind does.
record_split names split_into, and no other kind does.
record_replaced names replaced_by, and no other kind does.
Only a record_created has no previous_seq, and only it can name split_from.
A change that applies a submission names the decision that approved it.
A revert names the change it undoes and the decision that ordered it.
A takedown names its reason and the decision. Like every change it never names a submission, so the requester is never exposed.
A recompute changes derived values only, names its reason, and has no decision. derived_updated comes only from a recompute.
